h2: Pool Repair Kerobokan & Umalas – Leaks, Tiles & Pipework
intro: Most villas in Kerobokan Kelod and Umalas were built 15–20 years ago, so pool shells, grout lines and pipework are reaching the point where small issues quietly become bigger ones. Bali Fix takes care of the pool repair jobs Kerobokan & Umalas villa owners call about most often — leak detection, loose mosaic tiles, re-grouting and pipe fixes — without tearing up your garden.

sections.h3: Why Pools Here Age Differently Than in Newer Builds
sections.text: In Kerobokan Kaja and Banjar Anyar you'll notice older villas sitting right next to 2020s builds. That mix means I see cracked 18-year-old shells alongside brand-new tile work with poor initial sealing. Families living full-time put steady pressure on pumps, heaters and septic lines, while the high groundwater table from nearby rice fields pushes moisture into drains after every heavy rain. I assess all of that together so you fix what actually matters first instead of chasing symptoms.

sections.h3: What We Usually Find in Kerobokan & Umalas Pools
sections.text: The most common calls from Umalas are a pool losing half a centimetre of water per day with no visible crack, mosaic tiles popping up around the skimmer or steps, grout turning white-powdery after two wet seasons, and a slow drip at a pipe joint under the deck. Bigger gardens in these areas also mean irrigation lines and drainage channels need checking alongside the pool itself. I walk through each issue on site and tell you which one to tackle before the next rainy week.

sections.h3: Send Photos on WhatsApp Before Booking
sections.text: Before we book anything, send me two or three photos on WhatsApp showing the problem area — a close-up of the loose tile, the wet patch under the deck, or the grout line that's crumbling. Add a sentence about how long it's been happening and whether your water level is dropping. That's enough for me to give you a rough idea of scope and what the visit will involve. The final quote depends on what I find once I'm on site, so no surprises.

Because this part of Bali sits in a high-water-table zone, a few habits save you from repeat calls. Check your grout lines every dry season — if it crumbles between your fingers, re-grout before the next wet months hit. Keep an eye on water level weekly; a steady drop of more than a centimetre a day is worth flagging early. If your villa has been empty for a couple of weeks, run the pump and open the drain valve to flush standing water out of the pipes.

faq.q: Do you handle both older pool shells and newer builds?
faq.a: Yes — I work on everything from 20-year-old concrete pools in Kerobokan Kaja to brand-new tile installations that were sealed poorly at handover.

faq.q: What if the leak source isn't obvious from photos?
faq.a: I'll do a visual inspection first, then use pressure testing or dye tracing as needed. You get a clear explanation of what I found before any work starts.

faq.q: Can you also check irrigation lines and garden drainage?
faq.a: Absolutely. In bigger Umalas gardens those systems share the same high-water-table issues as the pool, so it makes sense to look at them together during one visit.
